o1.biggest_strength: It is shootable tomorrow: aspect ratios, safe zones, headline character counts, labelled 'Mokobara review' lines, 'show no front pocket', and a sound-led Reel built on the 290-mention quiet-wheels theme.
o1.biggest_mistake: The first-three pick. Two of the three go at the same men's audience, and the lift-it-alone women's concept (22% of buyers, ₹1,058 a purchase) waits. Concepts 1 versus 2 also change angle and format together, so the result won't tell you which one worked.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Swap the second men's concept out for 'No asking for help', so the first three are quiet wheels, work flyers and women solo, and hold format constant in any pair you mean to compare.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads my data like an owner: women are 18% of spend but 26% of purchases, the ₹292-a-trip reframe for price, the ₹1,515 blended cost per purchase turned into a ₹4,500 learning budget, and the first three picks match where the money and the cheapest buyers actually are.
o2.biggest_mistake: Less shootable than it should be: no aspect ratios, safe zones or headline character counts, concept 3 says 'Everyone' instead of a named audience, and review lines sit in ad copy unlabelled, which risks reading as our own claim. Lines like 'zero belt time' also edge past the approved specs.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the one-page production spec sheet and label every review quote, then pin each concept to a named audience so a designer and a media buyer can both start on Monday without asking me anything.

reason: Both are usable, but I'd hand 2 to the team first: its three first picks line up with where the spend and the cheapest buyers are, and it tells me how much to spend before I judge a concept. I'd then bolt 1's production spec sheet and labelled review quotes onto it.
